notes: Parts are the same as in step 1; nothing added or dropped.
Circuit follows the tutorial text: pin 13 -> 220 ohm resistor -> LED anode (long leg); LED cathode (short leg) -> GND.

The resistor and LED are placed on the top half of the breadboard. Resistor leg 1 is in column 10 and leg 2 in column 14. The LED anode is in column 14, so it shares a strip with resistor leg 2. The cathode is in column 15, which the ground wire also uses.
Exact breadboard columns are chosen to match the circuit image roughly; the image only shows the layout, not hole labels.
The Uno's GND pin next to pin 13 is used as GND.1, as in the image where the black wire goes to the header beside pin 13.
Resistor value is 220 ohm, which keeps the current safe for a 5 V board with a red LED.
